title: Compact-source maps into finite-length semi-free modules have finite-cell support
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $A=\bigoplus_{j\in\mathbf Z}A^j$ be an associative unital graded ring with additive differential $d:A^j\to A^{j+1}$, $d^2=0$, and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^{|a|}a\,d(b)$. A right dg $A$-module is a graded right module $L$ with degree-one differential satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(xa)=d(x)a+(-1)^{|x|}x\,d(a)$. Let $D(A)$ be their homotopy category localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups, where homotopies satisfy $f-g=d h+h d$ for degree-minus-one graded right-linear maps $h$. Write $A[k]^j=A^{j+k}$ with differential $(-1)^k d_A$ and unchanged right action. Let $E\in D(A)$ be compact [def-pc-compact-object] for small coproducts represented by direct sums. Let $n\geq0$ and let $T$ be a right dg $A$-module with a specified finite filtration $0=F_{-1}T\subseteq F_0T\subseteq\cdots\subseteq F_nT=T$ by dg submodules and specified dg isomorphisms $F_iT/F_{i-1}T\cong\bigoplus_{j\in J_i}A[k_{ij}]$ for $0\leq i\leq n$, small sets $J_i$ and integers $k_{ij}$. For every morphism $f:E\to T$ in $D(A)$ there exist a dg submodule $T'\subseteq T$, finite subsets $J'_i\subseteq J_i$, and a morphism $g:E\to T'$ in $D(A)$ such that $f$ is $g$ followed by the inclusion $T'\hookrightarrow T$, and such that the injection
$$ (F_iT\cap T')/(F_{i-1}T\cap T')\longrightarrow F_iT/F_{i-1}T $$
has image exactly $\bigoplus_{j\in J'_i}A[k_{ij}]$ under the specified isomorphism. In particular these quotient maps identify the successive quotients with finite sums of shifts of $A$. Empty index sets and $T=0$ are allowed; no boundedness, commutativity, flatness or countability hypothesis on $A$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, statement and finite-filtration induction; indices rewritten so that every layer, including F_0/F_{-1}, is covered.

proof.text: We descend on $m=n,n-1,\ldots,-1$. The induction assertion is that there is a DG submodule $U\subseteq T$ containing $F_mT$, a map $a:E\to U$ whose composite into $T$ is $f$, and finite subsets $S_i\subseteq J_i$ for $i>m$, such that the image of $(U\cap F_iT)/(U\cap F_{i-1}T)$ in the specified layer is exactly the coordinate subsum on $S_i$. For $m=n$ take $U=T$, $a=f$; there are no conditions on higher layers. At $m=-1$ this assertion is exactly the conclusion, since $F_{-1}T=0$. We construct the step from any $m\geq0$ to $m-1$ below.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, descending induction assertion and base case; layer indices shifted to cover F_0T.

proof.text: For each $i>m$ and $j\in S_i$, lift the standard homogeneous generator of $A[k_{ij}]$ to $x_{ij}\in U\cap F_iT$, of degree $-k_{ij}$. There are finitely many such lifts. Successively subtract their multiples in layers $n,n-1,\ldots,m+1$. This expresses every element of $U$ uniquely as an element of $F_mT$ plus a sum of their multiples: existence follows by killing its top layer at each subtraction, and uniqueness by projecting a relation to its highest nonzero layer, where the specified generators form a free graded basis. Thus, as graded modules, $U=F_mT\oplus\bigoplus_{i>m,j\in S_i}x_{ij}A$, and $U\cap F_lT=F_mT\oplus\bigoplus_{m<i\leq l,j\in S_i}x_{ij}A$ for $l\geq m$. Since the quotient generator is closed, $d(x_{ij})\in U\cap F_{i-1}T$. The same subtraction expresses it as $y_{ij}+\sum_{m<r<i,s\in S_r}x_{rs}b_{ij}^{rs}$, with $y_{ij}\in F_mT$ and homogeneous coefficients (each sum finite). These assertions concern the underlying graded modules only; the lifts need not be closed.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, homogeneous lifts and differential expansions; degree of the generator is -k with A[k]^j=A^{j+k}.

proof.text: Let $K\subseteq J_m$ be the union of the supports of the images of all $y_{ij}$ in $F_mT/F_{m-1}T=\bigoplus_{j\in J_m}A[k_{mj}]$. It is finite because there are finitely many $y_{ij}$ and each direct-sum element has finite support. Let $H_K\subseteq F_mT$ be the inverse image of the coordinate subsum on $K$, and set $V_K=H_K+\sum_{i>m,j\in S_i}x_{ij}A\subseteq U$. The subsum is a DG submodule, hence so is $H_K$. The displayed expansions give $d(x_{ij})\in V_K$, and $d(x_{ij}b)=d(x_{ij})b+(-1)^{|x_{ij}|}x_{ij}d(b)$ proves that $V_K$ is a DG submodule. The unique expansion in the previous step gives $V_K\cap F_mT=H_K$ and $V_K\cap F_lT=H_K\oplus\bigoplus_{m<i\leq l,j\in S_i}x_{ij}A$ for $l\geq m$. Its layer $m$ is precisely the coordinate subsum on $K$; its higher layers retain precisely $S_i$. It contains $F_{m-1}T$.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, finite supports, inverse-image submodule, and construction P double-prime plus the selected lifts.

proof.text: The inclusion $F_mT\to U$ induces a DG isomorphism $F_mT/H_K\xrightarrow{\sim}U/V_K$: it is surjective since the $x_{ij}$ are killed, and its kernel is $H_K$ by uniqueness of the graded expansion. Consequently $Q_K=U/V_K$ identifies as a DG module with $\bigoplus_{j\in J_m\setminus K}A[k_{mj}]$. Denote the quotient by $q_K:U\to Q_K$. For every remaining generator choose a homogeneous lift in $F_mT$; right-linear extension is a graded section of $q_K$. Thus $0\to V_K\to U\xrightarrow{q_K}Q_K\to0$ is graded-split. These lifts are not asserted to give a DG section. For any finite enlargement $L\supseteq K$, the same construction works, $V_K\subseteq V_L$, and the quotient map $U\to Q_L$ is $q_K$ followed by the coordinate projection deleting the summands indexed by $L\setminus K$.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, displayed complementary quotient; graded splitting made explicit by lifting its homogeneous free generators.

proof.text: Apply compactness [def-pc-compact-object] to $q_Ka:E\to Q_K$, using the coproduct represented by the stated DG direct sum. Its definition writes $q_Ka=\sum_{j\in B}\iota_j c_j$ for a finite subset $B\subseteq J_m\setminus K$ and morphisms $c_j:E\to A[k_{mj}]$. Put $L=K\cup B$. The coordinate projection $Q_K\to Q_L$ kills every displayed $\iota_j$, so $q_La=0$. The module $V_L$ has exactly the layer properties already verified for $V_K$, now with layer $m$ indexed by $L$.

source.place: Tag 09R2, lemma-factor-through-nicer, compactness and finite enlargement; derived.tex Tag 07LS, definition-compact-object.

proof.text: The graded-split sequence $0\to V_L\to U\xrightarrow{q_L}Q_L\to0$ gives a distinguished triangle $V_L\to U\xrightarrow{q_L}Q_L\to V_L[1]$ by [lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles]. Its first two arrows are the actual inclusion and quotient. Since $q_La=0$, clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-hom-into-triangle-exact] gives $b:E\to V_L$ whose composite into $U$ is $a$. Therefore its composite into $T$ is $f$. Replace $U,a$ by $V_L,b$, retain $S_i$ for $i>m$, and take $S_m=L$. This proves the induction step. After the finite descent to $m=-1$, put $T'=U$, $g=a$, and $J'_i=S_i$. All quotient images are the specified coordinate subsums, not merely abstract isomorphic sums. The construction allows every selected set to be empty. When $T=0$ it gives $T'=0$ and the zero factorization.
